1.21.1.0.763.0:
### 0.763.0

**Menu changes**

Some tidying on the main menu.

**Your leaderboard position keeps up with you**

A leaderboard book ends by telling you where you stand on that board. That position was worked out once, when you joined, and never again — so on a long session it slowly went stale, and a book you found late in the evening could still be quoting the number you had hours earlier. Your standing is now looked up again after each death, which is the moment it actually moves.

- Leaderboard books quote a current position, not the one you joined with
- Your standing is looked up again after each death
1.21.1.0.762.0:
### 0.762.0

**Friends you kill no longer count as friends you made**

Befriending a passenger and then killing them used to leave them counted on both sides of the ledger — they stayed in your friends made tally on the death screen, in your lifetime total, in your stat book and on the leaderboard. Now a kill takes them out of it. The kill itself still counts.

- Killing a passenger removes them from your friends made count for that run.
- If the passenger you killed was your closest friend, the death-screen friend portrait moves to whoever is still alive and likes you most.

### 0.761.0

**Smoother carriage catch-up, and carriages that no longer touch**

When the train gets ahead of you — or rolls past while you stand still — it adds the carriages it is missing one at a time over successive moments, instead of dropping the whole missing stretch in at once. Catching up now happens just as quickly without the brief stutter it used to cost. Freshly appeared carriages also settle straight into place: the game had been judging the gap to a new carriage's neighbour before that carriage had finished moving into position, which could shunt it around and leave two carriages briefly touching.

- Catching up no longer causes a visible stutter, however far behind the train has fallen
- New carriages no longer end up momentarily touching the one in front
- Carriages settle into place first time instead of being nudged back and forth
- Catch-up spawning can be set to Off, Burst 2, or Fill all under Options → Dungeon Train → Train

### 0.760.0

**Star the builds and builders you want to find again**

My Builds now has a star on every build, and a Favourites screen listing everything you have starred. A star is private — nobody else sees it, nothing is counted, and no build is ranked by it. It simply follows you: star something on one machine and it is starred on the next, because your favourites live with your builder profile rather than in that world's files.

- A star on every tile in My Builds, and a Starred filter to narrow the grid to just those
- A Favourites screen collecting everything you have starred, with Load into Editor to pull one back into your library
- Your stars are private and uncounted — this is a bookmark, not a vote
- Favourites follow your profile between worlds and machines

### 0.759.0

**Loading one of your own builds back is a shorter question**

Loading a build from My Builds now ends with you standing at it: the menu closes and the editor takes you to the template, even if you weren't in an editor plot when you started. When the name is already in use, the question fits on screen and comes in two halves — New loads it under a fresh name, or Replace Existing asks whether to keep a copy of the build you have or overwrite it.

- A load finishes at the build, not at the menu you started from
- The name-clash question no longer runs off the edge of the screen
- New / Replace Existing, with keep-a-copy or overwrite behind the second

### 0.758.0

**Saving a build you've submitted always syncs**

Saving a template in the Train Editor could tell you it was "out on someone's train" and quietly skip the upload to My Builds — and saying it would sync next time was wrong, because every later save stopped in the same place. Your own saves no longer wait for anyone: they go straight to your build, whoever happens to be riding it.

- An editor or builder save always reaches My Builds, even for a build you've submitted for review
- Nobody riding a build is interrupted by its author saving it

**The train catches up when it gets ahead of you**

When the train outran you — you sprinted ahead, or it rolled past while you stood still — its ends could only grow back one group of carriages at a time, so a fast train just left you behind. Each end now fills in every carriage it is missing the moment it falls behind, and settles back to its normal pace once it has caught up. A new Catch-up spawning setting under Options → Dungeon Train → Train chooses how hard it tries: Fill all, the default, keeps adding carriages every moment until the train has caught up; Burst 2 adds two at a time for a gentler catch-up; and Off keeps the old one-group-at-a-time pace. It applies to the train you are already riding.

- Train ends fill back in when they fall behind, instead of letting a fast train run away from you
- New Catch-up spawning setting in Options → Dungeon Train → Train — Fill all (default), Burst 2, or Off
- Carriage gaps stay even while catching up — groups added together move as one unit until they settle

### 0.757.0

**Loading your own build from My Builds works again**

Loading one of your own builds back from My Builds could refuse with "you already have a build by that name here" when you didn't. Any name Dungeon Train itself ships counted as one you already had — which is every sub-variant of a contents group, so those could never be loaded at all. Your own builds now load; a build by somebody else still asks before it replaces anything built in. Loading a dimensional carriage also opens it properly instead of failing with "Unknown dimensional carriage" straight after downloading it.

- Your own builds load from My Builds even when the name matches one Dungeon Train ships
- Contents sub-variants can be loaded at all — every one of them was blocked
- A downloaded dimensional carriage opens in the editor and shows up in the list right away

### 0.756.0

**Translation editor catches a book losing its numbers**

When you translate a story book in the in-game translation editor, the editor now tells you if your text has lost one of the numbers the game fills in — the death count in an epitaph, the carriage you fell in. Those are written as {deaths} or {deaths_nth} in the English, and until now nothing noticed when one went missing on the way through: the line would ship with the number simply gone. Only bracketed figures are checked, so a percent sign or a stray brace in a story is still just prose.

- The editor names the missing figure while you are still typing
- Approved translations that lost a figure are held back instead of shipped

### 0.754.0

**More editors count as cheat mods**

Installing Visual Mobs Edit or In-game NBTEdit Reborn now puts the run into Free Play. One rewrites mob health, damage, immunities and spawn rules from a menu — the difficulty curve a run is measured against — and the other rewrites the NBT of whatever you are holding or looking at.

- Visual Mobs Edit and In-game NBTEdit Reborn added to the cheat-mod list

### 0.753.0

**Internal tooling**

Development tooling changes.
1.21.1.0.752.0:
### 0.752.0

**In-game editors count as cheat mods**

Installing CAD Editor, DINE or AnkiNBT now puts the run into Free Play, alongside the other in-game editors. They rewrite an item's components, a mob or block entity's NBT, or a villager's trades from a GUI, so they do the work of a command without one.

- CAD Editor, DINE and AnkiNBT added to the cheat-mod list

### 0.751.0

**Smoother world join**

Starting a world now fades from the menu into the loading screen instead of cutting, with no more flash of vanilla chrome.

**Big endless rooms stop rebuilding themselves on the spot**

A large endless portal room used to rebuild one of its copies every tick — tearing one down and putting another up — for as long as anyone was standing in it. It now settles once the room is fully built around you, and only moves copies when you actually walk.

- Standing still in a big endless room no longer churns the server
- Walking still opens the room ahead of you exactly as before
1.21.1.0.750.0:
### 0.750.0

**Translators ranked by how much they translated**

The Credits page now lists translators biggest-contribution-first, counting everything a person has translated across every language they worked on. Volunteers whose work is serving live from the relay rank alongside those already baked into the build, so the person who translated the most of the mod is at the top of the card rather than at the bottom of it.

- Credits ranks translators by total lines translated, not by arrival order
- Work approved since the last release now ranks equally with work shipped in the jar
- Each translator's languages are listed strongest-first

### 0.749.0

**Rooms with a moved doorway build in full, and stay built**

A dimensional carriage whose doorway had been moved off the room's floor was being stamped partly outside the world, so the bottom of the room simply never appeared — the author walked into the top of their own build standing on nothing. Those rooms now stand on solid ground, keep their endless copies while you walk through them, and are fogged and lit all the way down.

- A room with a raised doorway builds every row the author made, instead of losing everything below the world's floor
- Endless rooms no longer shed their copies around a player standing on the room's own floor
- Fog and daylight now fill the whole room, rather than stopping at the corridor's floor line
- Test the Carriage says so when a room is too tall for the world you are testing it in, instead of failing

### 0.748.0

**Editor mirroring follows the template you build into**

Template mirroring now keys off the block you place, not where you are standing. Building into a mirror-enabled template from its roof, from the gap between plots, or from a neighbouring plot is mirrored using that template's own settings — previously those edits silently lost their mirror image.

- Mirroring works when you build into a template from outside it
- Each template's own mirror axes apply, even while you stand in a neighbouring plot

### 0.747.0

**Player translations no longer blocked by a single mistyped one**

The weekly job that pulls player-submitted translations into the mod was still stopping dead on one bad submission out of 1,790 — a Russian line that had lost one of its two fill-in slots. Everything else, more than a thousand approved translations, was thrown away with it. A submission that would not display correctly is now set aside and named, and the rest are imported.

- One malformed submission no longer discards the other 1,100
- A translation that loses or gains a fill-in slot is set aside with the reason, so it can be corrected rather than silently shipped broken
- Closed a crash route: a stray percent sign in a submitted translation would have taken down whichever screen showed it

### 0.746.0

**The translation editor now catches a broken placeholder as you type**

When you translate the game from inside the game, some lines contain slots the game fills in — a player's name, a number, a key binding. Dropping one, adding one, or typing a lone percent sign makes that line display wrongly or not at all, and until now nothing said so: the mistake was only found weeks later, when the translation was pulled into the mod and quietly set aside. The editor now tells you the moment you type it, names the slot you have lost, and holds Save until it is right.

- A missing or invented fill-in slot is flagged under the text box as you type
- Save is held until the line will actually display, so no more work is lost weeks later
- Reordering slots to suit your language is still fine — only losing or inventing them is not

### 0.745.0

**Internal tooling**

Development tooling changes.

### 0.744.0

**Growing a portal room gives you empty space, not a room you have to demolish**

Resizing a dimensional carriage in the editor used to fill the new space with the built-in room — a floor, walls, a ceiling and its lights — so every step of the size dial handed you blocks you then had to clear out. New space now arrives as plain air, ready to build in. The one thing that still comes back is what you cropped: shrink past something and step back up, and the row returns exactly as it was, blocks, decoration, chests and all.

- Growing a dimensional carriage now opens empty space instead of stamping the built-in room into it
- Shrinking then growing still restores the row you cropped, unchanged

### 0.743.0

**Testing a dimensional carriage offers to save it first**

Test the Carriage stamps the room from its last save, so an unsaved edit was quietly missing from the room you walked into. It now offers to save that one carriage first — save and test, or test the saved version anyway. A carriage with nothing to save goes straight in, as before.

- Test the Carriage asks to save when the room you are standing in has unsaved changes
- Catches an unsaved resize as well as unsaved blocks

### 0.741.0

**The loading screen starts themed**

Opening a world no longer flashes the main-menu panorama before the Dungeon Train loading screen appears — the themed screen is there from the first frame of the load.

- The world-open screens are themed, so the join starts on the train panel instead of vanilla chrome
1.21.1.0.742.0:
### 0.741.0

**Your backpack is there when you open a chest**

Until now the backpack only existed on your own inventory screen, so opening a chest made it vanish — moving a stack between the two meant closing the chest, opening your inventory, dragging, and opening the chest again. The panels now sit either side of chests, ender chests, barrels and shulker boxes as well, and shift-click moves stacks straight between the container, your inventory and the backpack. Shift-clicking out of the backpack puts things in the chest, the way a shift-click in a chest always has. The open/close button is also smaller and quieter, and now shows at a glance whether the backpack is open.

- Backpack panels appear in chests, ender chests, barrels and shulker boxes
- Shift-click moves stacks between the container, your inventory and the backpack in one click
- Shift-clicking out of the backpack deposits into the container, falling back to your inventory when it is full
- The open/close button is smaller, and its icon dims while the backpack is shut

**The portal room's two doorways now say which is which**

Building a portal room, the two corridor doorways used to be identical amber outlines, so there was no way to tell the way in from the way out until you had already clicked one. The entrance is now blue and the exit yellow, and standing near either one names it.

- Entrance and Exit labels float over the doorway you are standing at
- The entry mouth is drawn blue, the exit yellow, at any distance

**The loading screen starts themed**

Opening a world no longer flashes the main-menu panorama before the Dungeon Train loading screen appears — the themed screen is there from the first frame of the load.

- The world-open screens are themed, so the join starts on the train panel instead of vanilla chrome

### 0.740.0

**Item names match the item again in Vietnamese, Filipino and Simplified Chinese**

Three languages were drawing item-name synonyms from the whole pool instead of the right category, so a sword could end up called "Boots". They now name swords like swords and helmets like helmets, the way the other seventeen languages already did. Simplified Chinese also gained the Discord Presence screens — the consent prompt, the feedback survey and the chat auto-responses — which had been showing in English.

- Vietnamese, Filipino and Simplified Chinese item names now match the item's category
- Simplified Chinese: rebuilt the synonym list, which had drifted onto a different set of item categories
- Simplified Chinese: Discord Presence consent screen, feedback survey and chat replies are translated

### 0.739.0

**Submit a build for review, and see where it stands**

Submitting a build from My Builds now actually reaches a person. Your build waits in a review queue, and the screen tells you whether it is waiting, accepted, or not accepted — instead of quietly publishing and never mentioning it again. Only accepted builds can ride other players' trains.

- My Builds shows each build's review state as a coloured badge in the corner of its tile
- Filter your builds by kind and by review state, and choose how many fit in a row
- A build that wasn't accepted says so, so you can change it and submit it again

**Nineteen languages stop falling back to English, and player translations flow again**

Every language except English was missing the same 144 pieces of interface text — the data-recovery screen, the backup options, the abandon-run confirmation, twelve advancements and the leaderboard headers all read in English no matter what language you play in. All 144 are now translated in all 20 languages. The same gap had also jammed the weekly job that pulls player-submitted translations back into the mod: it had never once succeeded, because 198 approved submissions had nowhere to land and took 979 good ones down with them every time it ran.

- 144 missing strings translated into all 20 languages — 2,850 in total
- Player-approved translations import again: 1,102 that were being discarded now land, and anything that cannot is listed by name instead of failing the whole run
- The in-game translation editor no longer asks you for plural forms your language does not have — Russian was being shown 27 of them
- Fixed a crash on the AI-policy screen caused by an unescaped percent sign in the English text
- Three buttons in the editor settings showed raw key names in English; the note markers on one story letter pointed past the end of the translated text in five languages

### 0.738.0

**The opening ramp is half as long**

Your first ride used to spend 25 carriages easing you in — nothing hostile at all for the first 10, then only small slimes for another 15. That is now 10 carriages: no hostiles through carriage 5, slimes through carriage 10, and the real mobs from there. Starter-tier chest loot follows the same window, so the gentle stretch stays consistent and then gets out of your way.

- No hostiles for the first 5 carriages (was 10)
- Small slimes for carriages 5-10 (was 10-25)
- Authored mobs — and their proper chest loot — from carriage 10 instead of 25

**The loading screen now hands you the shot**

Joining a run reads as one continuous themed loading screen — no more flash back to a vanilla screen when the world finishes loading and the train starts. Once the bar fills it says "All Aboard!", the panel fades away over 30 seconds into a dim over the live world, and the camera is already sitting exactly where the arrival shot begins, so pressing Space flies you in from the frame you were looking at. The train's engine now eases in from silence instead of arriving at full volume.

- The world-join loading screen no longer flashes back to the vanilla "Downloading terrain" panorama
- At 100% the screen reads "All Aboard!" and slowly reveals the composed arrival shot behind a dim
- The train engine ambient fades in over 30 seconds when you first come aboard

### 0.737.0

**Crash Assistant now ships with the modpack**

If the game ever crashes, a window now opens explaining what went wrong — it checks your logs against dozens of known causes, from graphics-driver faults to running out of memory. One button uploads every relevant log and hands you a ready-to-paste report, and the help button drops you straight into #bugs-feedback on the Dungeon Train Discord.

- A post-crash window that diagnoses dozens of common crash causes
- One click uploads every log and gives you a ready-to-paste report
- Takes you straight to #bugs-feedback on the Dungeon Train Discord
- Client-side only — dedicated servers are unaffected

### 0.736.0

**New translators are credited without a manual step**

When someone translates part of the game for the first time, the weekly job that pulls approved player translations back into the mod used to stop dead until a maintainer added that person to the credits registry by hand. It now adds them itself, as part of the same change a human reviews and approves — so a new translator's work no longer waits on a round trip nobody is scheduled to make.

- A first-time translator no longer blocks the whole week's import
- New names are added only once their work has actually landed, and are listed for review
- Work credited to a machine is still refused outright

### 0.734.0

**Dimensional carriage doorways can be placed independently**

A dimensional carriage's two doorways no longer have to line up. Builders can put the way in and the way out at different points along a room's wall and at different heights, so a portal room can bend your path instead of running you straight through it. Place a door on the mouth you want to move and only that mouth moves; rooms built before this keep both doorways where they were.

- Set each of a portal room's two doorways separately — along the wall and up it
- Aim a door at the near opening to move the way in, the far one to move the way out
- Fixed doorways that could be bricked over at the top, or leave a gap to the rock below, when a door was raised off the room's floor
1.21.1.0.732.0:
### 0.729.0

**Shulker boxes near dimensional carriages**

Shulker boxes can no longer be placed inside rooms adjacent to a dimensional carriage. Dimensional carriages themselves are unaffected.

### 0.728.0

**AI Policy page redesign**

The AI Policy page is easier to read at a glance. Each section is now its own card with a coloured heading, and every point carries an item icon — green for the things made by hand, amber for where AI is actually used. Long pages also get a scrollbar.

- AI Policy sections are now cards with colour-coded headings
- Every point carries an item icon
- Added a scrollbar to the page

### 0.727.0

**AI Policy screen**

A new in-game page states plainly what in Dungeon Train is made by hand and where AI is actually used. The books, the artwork, the player mobs and the name generator are not AI; nothing is trained on your data, and no AI runs on your machine. Open it from Dungeon Train Options, or from the paper icon on the Credits page.

- New AI Policy page — what is and is not made by AI, in plain terms
- Reachable from Dungeon Train Options and from the Credits page
- Links out to the Discord updates channel

### 0.726.0

**Traps are remembered**

Setting a trap in a drifting carriage, for whoever comes through next, leaves a mark on the temperament your echo is born with.

### 0.725.0

**Dimensional carriage doorways can be moved off centre**

The two doorways into a dimensional carriage used to be pinned to the exact middle of the room's end walls, at floor level, on every room ever built. Builders can now put them where they want: hold a door and right-click the doorway marker, and both doorways move to where you aimed — along the wall and up it. Nothing is placed; the door in your hand is just a pointer, which is what lets a doorway sit anywhere rather than only where a door would have something to stand on. How far it can move depends on how much bigger the room is than the corridor running into it, since the corridor still has to be sealed inside the room's walls — a room built at the smallest legal size has nowhere to move it to, and the game now tells you that, and what to grow to get the room.

- Hold a door and right-click a doorway marker to set where the doorways sit
- Doorways move both across the end wall and up it
- Wider and taller rooms give the doorways more room to move
- Rooms built before this are untouched — their doorways stay exactly where they were

1.21.1.0.725.0:
### 0.725.0

**Portal corridors fade instead of switching at the door**

Walking a portal carriage now changes over the whole walk rather than in the single step through the far door. The fog, the corridor's own light and a daylit room's brightness all shift together as you go, easing in as you leave the train and settling a block before you reach the room — so arriving is a non-event instead of a visible switch.

- Fog and lighting now shift across the whole corridor, not at the doorway
- Eased at both ends, so leaving the train and reaching the room are both gentle
- The step through the portal room's door no longer changes what you see

### 0.724.0

**Durability numbers on item tooltips**

The modpack now ships Durability Tooltip, switched on by default: hover any tool, weapon or piece of armour and its remaining durability is written out as a number — 'Durability: 137 / 250' — coloured green through orange to red as it wears down, instead of squinting at the damage bar. Its required library, SuperMartijn642's Config Lib, ships alongside it. You can change the style to a bar or plain words, or turn it off, in the mod's config.

- Durability Tooltip bundled and enabled by default
- Remaining durability shown as coloured numbers on tool, weapon and armour tooltips

### 0.723.0

**Enchantment tooltips now explain what each enchantment does**

The modpack now ships Enchantment Descriptions, switched on by default. Hover any enchanted item and each enchantment carries a short plain-English line explaining what it actually does — handy when a train chest hands you something you've never rolled before. Its two library dependencies, Bookshelf and Prickle, ship enabled alongside it.

- Enchantment Descriptions bundled and enabled by default
- Enchanted item tooltips now explain each enchantment's effect

### 0.722.0

**End cities are rarer**

End cities in the End band now generate about 5× less often.

**Difficulty potion effects now show as infinite**

Buffed mobs on the train carry their difficulty potion effects permanently, but the effect readout showed a nonsensical multi-thousand-hour countdown instead of the infinity symbol. The effects were always meant to be permanent — now they are marked as such, so Jade and the vanilla effect display both read the infinity symbol.

- Difficulty potion effects on train mobs read as infinite instead of an absurd hour count

### 0.721.0

**Advancement tweaks**

A few advancement adjustments.

### 0.720.0

**Fixed mobs getting stuck behind in endless dimensional carriage rooms**

Mobs that wandered into a room copy that later retired could get left behind instead of being cleaned up. Fixed.

### 0.719.0

**The upside-down world is upside-down again — with shaders on**

If you play with Sodium or Iris shaders — which the modpack ships — the upside-down stretch was quietly rendering the right way up. The world now hangs from the ceiling as it should, whether or not a shaderpack is loaded, while the train stays upright underneath you.

- Fixed: upside-down band terrain rendered upright for anyone running Sodium or Iris shaders
- The flip now looks identical with shaders on and off
- Terrain right beside the track flips too, not just the far hills
1.21.1.0.715.0:
### 0.715.0

**Abandoning a run now asks first**

The pause menu's red "Abandon This Run" button used to kill you on the first click. It now asks, and says outright what abandoning means: your character dies, it counts as a death, and there is no undo.

- A confirmation step between the button and the kill — no more losing a long run to a stray click.
- Escape or "Go back" leaves the run exactly as it was; only the red confirm ends it.
1.21.1.0.714.0:
### 0.714.0

**Leaderboards now start from scores the game can vouch for**

The last update stopped Free Play runs from being ranked, but it could only do that for runs recorded after it shipped — every score already on a board predated the check, including a 29,999,728m walk that was really a flight to the edge of the world. Rather than delete anyone's history, those scores are now kept but unranked, and the boards rebuild from runs the game can actually vouch for. Expect the one-life boards to look sparse at first and fill in over the following days as players update and finish a run. Most Books Written and Most Advancements are unaffected, because those are counted by the server rather than reported by the game. Nothing has been erased — your stats, death records and Stat Room shelves are all exactly as they were.

- Old scores are retained but no longer ranked, including the bogus ones
- Boards refill from verified runs over the days after this update
- Most Books Written and Most Advancements are unchanged
- Playing on an older version means your runs won't be ranked until you update

### 0.713.0

**Armor trim templates are finally worth trading**

Pulling a Silence or Wayfinder template out of a carriage felt like a find, and then the villager offered you a single item for it — the same as a stick. Minecraft marks every armor trim template as ordinary, so Trade Everything had been pricing them at the bare minimum. They are now worth 2.2 emeralds apiece in the Trade Anything slot, which works out to 26 items in trade. All eighteen templates, including Flow and Bolt.

- Every armor trim smithing template now values at 2.2 emeralds, up from 1/16th
- Covers all eighteen, and any a datapack adds
- The Netherite upgrade template is untouched — it is not an armor trim
- Only applies when Trade Everything is installed; it ships with the modpack

### 0.712.0

**The leaderboards are for real runs again**

Someone in Free Play could fly to the edge of the world and take the top of a leaderboard with it. "Furthest Distance, One Life" was led by a 29,999,728m walk that nobody walked. Free Play runs no longer score on any board — the game already knew a run had gone into creative, it just wasn't telling the leaderboards. Your own stats and death records are unaffected, and Free Play still works exactly as it did; it simply stops competing with people playing it straight. The one-life boards were the ones affected: distance, time aboard, carriages reached, chests opened, pacifist run, friends made, echoes put down, and walking past the loot. The all-lives boards were already safe.

- Free Play runs are no longer ranked on any leaderboard
- The bogus world-border distance records are being removed
- Nothing changes about how Free Play itself plays

### 0.711.0

**Two runaway relay requests that were costing you frame time**

Standing in a Stat Room, or riding past a community carriage, was quietly making the game ask the server the same thing over and over — twenty times a second, for the rest of the session. Two separate faults, both fixed. A Stat Room waiting on a leaderboard the server has no scores for yet now waits politely instead of asking on every tick, and a community carriage you have never touched no longer uploads a copy of itself moments after it appears. If reactions felt sluggish lately — chests opening slowly, hits not landing, items not picking up — this is a large part of why.

- Fixed: a leaderboard with no scores yet was re-requested every tick, forever
- Fixed: every community carriage uploaded itself on arrival, even untouched
- Stat Rooms still fill in as their boards arrive, just without the churn
- Your own edits to a community carriage still sync exactly as before

### 0.710.0

**Internal improvements**

Behind-the-scenes maintenance work. Nothing to see or do differently in game.

### 0.709.0

**Approved player translations flow back into the game automatically**

Translations players submit in-game and that get approved are served by the relay straight away, but until now they never made it into the mod itself — so they vanished on an offline launch and their authors went uncredited in the jar. A weekly job now pulls approved work back into the build for review.

- Approved player translations are collected weekly instead of by hand
- Translators must be registered with their credit before their work can be merged

### 0.708.0

**Turn the backpack button on or off**

The backpack panels' open/close button on your inventory screen can now be switched off from Dungeon Train's own options, and it is a little smaller than before. Hiding it costs you nothing: the panels still open with the Edible Backpacks key, which you can bind under Controls.

- A new Backpack Button setting under Options -> Dungeon Train... -> General shows or hides the button.
- The button itself is smaller, so it sits over the inventory without reading as another piece of GUI furniture.
- Shift-clicking an item now fills your hotbar and inventory first, and only overflows into the backpack panels.
- The Upgraded Backpack advancement now describes the real recipe: eight backpacks around a gold block.
1.21.1.0.706.0:
### 0.706.0

**Editor: category switching skips the save prompt**

The "Save before switch?" list flagged templates nobody had edited, so it is bypassed for now. Save with /dt save before switching — the switch re-stamps every plot.

### 0.705.0

**The carriage at the edge of view stops changing on you**

A single carriage near the edge of your render distance could quietly rebuild itself as a different type, from a different stage, when it reloaded. It now comes back as the carriage that was there. Carriages that slip out of line are also pulled back into place instead of being abandoned mid-train.

- A reloading carriage keeps the stage and the build it was made with, instead of re-rolling against wherever the train has since travelled.
- A carriage that ends up badly out of line is put back in one move, rather than inching toward the train and giving up.
- Carriages either side of one that is still settling keep moving with the train, so the two cannot drift apart while it beds in.

### 0.704.0

**Turn your own train builds on or off from the main menu**

If you have builds of your own from the Train Editor, the main menu now carries a switch for them, sitting just left of New Game. Lit means your designs ride the train — and those runs stay Free Play, so stats and advancements keep to that world. Grey means the built-in designs ride instead, and everything you do counts. Flipping it also settles the question for good: worlds stop stopping to ask which train you want. Options → Custom Train Content puts the question back if you'd rather be asked each time. The prompt itself now leads with the choice that keeps your stats.

- Main-menu switch for your own train builds, shown only when you have some
- Pressing it retires the per-world 'which train?' prompt
- That prompt now offers Default Train (Live) first
1.21.1.0.703.0:
### 0.703.0

**Control how many backups you keep, and clear them**

Dungeon Train keeps backups of your builds and progress, and until now it decided on its own how many to hold on to. It now keeps a set number per version — five by default — so you can tell at a glance what you have, and there is a button to delete them all and reclaim the space.

- A Backups section in Options > Dungeon Train, with a slider for how many backups to keep per version.
- Clear Backups shows how much disk your backups are using and deletes them, inside and outside your Minecraft folder, after confirming.

**TrashSlot now comes installed, and stays out of the way**

TrashSlot is now part of the pack proper rather than an optional extra you had to tick on. It ships quiet: there is no trash slot in your inventory and none of its keys are bound, so nothing about your screens or your controls changes unless you want it to. To use it, bind a key to Show/Hide TrashSlot under Options then Controls, and press it with a screen open.

- Installed with the pack — no optional-mods tick needed
- Ships with the slot hidden and every TrashSlot key unbound, so your inventory and controls look exactly as they did
- Bind Show/Hide TrashSlot in Options then Controls to turn it on

### 0.701.0

**Load your builds from your profile into the editor**

My Builds could always show you what you had made — including builds from another world, another save, or another machine — but it could never open one. Now it can. Load into Editor pulls the build down, puts it in your template library and takes you straight to it, switching the editor to the right category on the way. If you already have a build by that name, it asks what you want: replace the one you have, rename the one you have, or load this one under a new name.

- Load into Editor on the My Builds screen
- Works for builds this world has never seen — a new save, a reinstall, a new machine
- Every kind: carriages, groups, rooms, parts, track and portal rooms
- Takes you to the build when it lands, changing editor category if it has to
- A name you already use asks what to do instead of refusing

### 0.699.0

**Night and sunrise skybox blocks**

Two more skies to punch a window through to. The Night Skybox Block is night on both halves of the day: the stars wheel overhead and the moon crosses with the right phase, but the sun never comes up, so a room built around one stays under a night sky no matter what time it is outside. The Sunrise Skybox Block holds a permanent dawn and turns sideways the way the upside-down skybox does, with the sun and its glow sweeping right around the horizon instead of climbing, the moon trailing opposite and the stars turning with them.

- New Night Skybox Block: stars, moon and phase, and no sunrise ever
- New Sunrise Skybox Block: a dawn that orbits the horizon sideways
- Both work anywhere the other skybox blocks do, carriage walls included
1.21.1.0.698.0:
### 0.698.0

**TrashSlot joins the modpack**

The modpack now ships TrashSlot, an optional inventory trash slot for binning junk without hunting for lava. It arrives switched off — tick it on in the launcher's optional-mods list whenever you want it.

- Drag-and-drop trash slot on most inventory screens
- Off by default — opt in from the launcher, no reinstall needed

### 0.697.0

**The game now counts the time you spend building**

Hours in the Train Builder used to count for nothing — every stat Dungeon Train kept was about riding. Time spent building is now tracked and ranked, alongside a board for the builds you have had approved onto other people's trains.

- Time in a Train Builder world, and time up at the editor plots, both count towards your building time.
- Two new leaderboard books: Longest Building, and Most Builds Approved.
- A Stat Room now stocks more books to match.
1.21.1.0.696.0:
### 0.694.0

**Choose where your backups are kept**

Dungeon Train's backups of your builds and progress used to live inside your Minecraft instance. That is likely safe from a modpack update, but not always — and it is no protection at all if the instance itself is deleted or reset. There's now a Backups setting in Options > Dungeon Train: On keeps a copy outside the instance so nothing an update or a reinstall does can reach it, Instanced keeps them inside it, and Off turns them off.

- New Backups option in Options > Dungeon Train — On / Instanced / Off, with each choice explained when you hover it.
- On (the default) keeps a copy outside your Minecraft folder, so reinstalling or resetting the instance no longer loses your builds.
- Server owners can set backups without the in-game menu: launch with -Ddungeontrain.backups=off (or DUNGEONTRAIN_BACKUPS=off), which accepts on / instanced / off.

### 0.693.0

**Dungeon Train speaks Romanian**

Romanian joins the language list — the whole game, not just the menus: every screen, the item names, and all 57 in-game books. It is machine translation nobody has proofread yet, and the language list says so with the faded AI mark; if you read Romanian, the in-game translation editor is open and your fixes come back to everyone.

- Romanian (Română) is selectable in the vanilla language list
- Menus, HUD, advancements, item names and all 57 books translated
- Counts follow real Romanian grammar — 1 vagon, 3 vagoane, 20 de vagoane
- Marked AI-unreviewed, so every line is open for community correction
1.21.1.0.692.0:
### 0.692.0

**Your builds and progress now survive a modpack update**

Updating the modpack could delete every carriage you'd built in the Train Editor and every advancement you'd earned. Dungeon Train kept them in the config folder, and modpack launchers replace that folder when a pack updates. They now live alongside your worlds, where an update can't touch them, and your existing files are moved across automatically the first time you launch.

- Train Editor builds, advancements, stats and loadouts moved out of the config folder to a place modpack updates leave alone.
- Dungeon Train now keeps rolling backups of your builds and progress — when you load a world, when you save a build in the Train Editor, when you die, and when you leave.
- Already lost your builds to an update? At the title screen Dungeon Train will offer to restore them from a backup or from an older install on your PC. /dtbackup and /dtrestore do the same in-game.

### 0.691.0

**One more advancement**

There is one more advancement in the game.
1.21.1.0.690.0:
### 0.690.0

**Portal room editor plots are lit by the room's own sky**

Building a dimensional carriage no longer means building it in the dark. A room's Sky setting — Daylight, Day/Night, Nether or End — now lights its editor plot the same way it will light the room once it is riding the train, so what you author is what you get without walking a test session first. A new Plot Lighting switch in the editor's X-menu Settings tab turns it off for anyone who wants the unlit box back while they place their own light sources. Skybox blocks stopped casting a shadow, too: a hole punched through to the sky now lets light through it, which is what it looked like it should have been doing all along.

- A portal room's Sky setting now lights its editor plot
- Plot Lighting switch in the X-menu Settings tab (on by default)
- Skybox blocks let light through instead of shadowing the floor below

### 0.689.0

**Stats books burn after reading, like every other book**

Leaderboard boards and Faulthurst's notes were the only books on the train you could keep. They now catch fire once you've read them, the same as a random chest book — and a board found in a chest could never burn at all until now.

- Leaderboard books and Faulthurst stat notes burn after reading
- Fixed: a leaderboard book rolled from a chest was the one book in the game that could never burn
- A book nobody has picked up still won't ignite — a broken chest, or a Stat Room's shelves, stay safe

### 0.688.0

**Better Advancements support, and it ships with the modpack**

The modpack now bundles Better Advancements, which replaces the advancements screen with a zoomable, searchable one. Dungeon Train's advancement tree works properly inside it: advancements you have unlocked the path to show their real icon, unearned ones still keep their secrets — you get the hint, not the description, and not the criteria behind it either. Scrolling a tall tree now reaches the whole thing, with a little room past each end. If you play without Better Advancements nothing changes.

- Better Advancements bundled with the modpack, enabled by default
- The Dungeon Train advancement tree renders correctly in its screen
- Unearned advancements keep showing hints instead of spoilers
- Scrolling reaches the bottom of a tall advancement tree

**Clearing a dimensional carriage in the editor really clears it**

The editor's Clear on a dimensional carriage left the room standing: it wiped the plot and then stamped the built-in room straight back over it, and the block variants it said it had removed reappeared the next time the plot was stamped. Clear now leaves the plot empty inside its cage, keeps the room's authored size, and the variants it drops stay dropped.

- Clear empties the plot instead of replacing your build with the built-in room.
- Cleared block variants no longer come back on the next stamp.
- A cleared room now shows as unsaved, so saving makes the clear permanent.
1.21.1.0.686.0:
### 0.685.0

**Shulker Box Tooltip added to the modpack**

The modpack now ships Shulker Box Tooltip. Hover any shulker box — or other container item — to see what's inside without placing it down, which saves a lot of digging through loot on the train.

- Hover a shulker box to preview its contents
- Enabled by default; can be switched off in the launcher

### 0.684.0

**Dungeon Train options screen redone with tabs**

The Dungeon Train settings screen (Options → Dungeon Train…) no longer runs off the bottom of the window. Settings are now split across three tabs — General, Train and Editor — each scrolling on its own with Done always reachable.

- Three tabs instead of one long column: General, Train, Editor
- The list scrolls and Done stays reachable at any window size or GUI scale
- Internet Connection row temporarily removed (could not be turned back on)

**Choose how each editor menu appears**

The Train Editor's four menus can each be shown either as a panel floating in the world that you aim at, or as a window on your screen that you point at with the mouse. Pick per menu under Options > Dungeon Train > Editor, or from the X menu's own Options. The X and V menus act on the whole build, so they open on screen where the cursor is more precise. The C and Z menus edit a single block, so they stay out in the world beside the block you're editing.

- The X menu can be a floating in-world panel again — it became a screen window last update, and now that's a choice rather than the only option.
- The V, C and Z menus can all be screen windows with a free mouse cursor.
- Your hotbar keeps working while a screen menu is open, so the V menu's Swap still takes whatever block you're holding.
- Each menu remembers its own setting, and a change takes effect the next time you open that menu.

**Clumps bundled in the modpack**

Both modpacks now ship Clumps, which merges nearby XP orbs into one so big fights drop a single combined orb instead of a laggy spray. It is on by default but optional — you can disable it in your launcher if you prefer vanilla orbs.

- XP orbs merge together, reducing lag from big mob fights
- Enabled by default in the CurseForge and Modrinth packs; safe to turn off
1.21.1.0.683.0:
### 0.683.0

**Empty carriages no longer turn up in the train**

A leftover test template was shipping with the mod, and it could be picked for any carriage slot like a normal one. When it was, you got a completely empty carriage — no floor, no walls, no roof, nothing inside — a gap in the middle of the train you could fall straight through. It has been removed, so every carriage the train builds is a real one.

- Removed the empty test carriage from the pool of carriages the train can build
- It no longer appears as a blank template in the carriage editor

**Builds are submitted for review**

Your saved builds go to your builder profile on the server, and a finished carriage can be submitted for review. Community carriages are paused on the train in the meantime.
1.21.1.0.682.0:
### 0.682.0

**The editor menu is now a proper screen, with tabs**

Pressing X in the editor opens a real menu with a mouse cursor instead of a panel floating in the world that you aimed your head at. Its rows are grouped into four tabs — File, Current, Settings and Nav — so you are not scanning thirty rows to find one. Your hotbar stays live underneath, so you can still pick the block a row is about to use.

- Point and click with a cursor — no more aiming your head at a floating panel
- Rows grouped into File, Current, Settings and Nav; tabs with nothing in them are hidden
- The hotbar keeps working while the menu is open — scroll it or press 1-9
- Long lists scroll instead of running off the bottom of the screen

### 0.681.0

**Finish and sign books left on ordinary lecterns**

A book & quill you leave on a plain lectern is now a draft you can come back to: right-click the lectern empty-handed to pick it up and keep writing, then sign it to seal it as a letter. Pressing Done leaves the book on the lectern exactly as you wrote it — your text is kept, nothing is handed back to you, and the book is no longer renamed behind your back.

- Right-click a lectern empty-handed to pick a draft back up and finish it
- Done keeps the text you just typed instead of discarding it
- Drafts rest on the lectern unchanged — no surprise rename, and no duplicate book in creative
1.21.1.0.681.0:
### 0.681.0

**No more ice pillars in the End band**

Stray towers of packed ice no longer generate beside the track when the train crosses the End band. The band's void chunks skipped their terrain fill but still ran the surface pass, so a frozen ocean underneath could stamp iceberg pillars into the void — and the strip of world that protects the track from the erosion kept them standing right where you ride past.

- The End band is clean void, islands and chorus again — no ice

### 0.680.0

**Cheats being available is Free Play**

A world where cheats are available to anyone playing is now Free Play for as long as that is true — advancements still earn live, but they don't add to your profile and global stats don't accrue. If you had cheats yourself, your run stays Free Play afterwards.

**Shift-click twice in the creative menu to fill your hotbar**

Shift-clicking an item in the creative menu still hands you a full stack on the cursor. Shift-click the same item again and that stack drops straight into your hotbar - and keep clicking to fill the slots along from there.

- The second shift-click on an item puts the stack in your hotbar: your selected slot if it is free, otherwise the first empty one.
- Every further click on that same item fills the next slot along, wrapping around to the start.
- Clicking a different item starts over, and the first shift-click behaves exactly as it always has.

### 0.679.0

**No weather in the End band**

Rain and lightning no longer follow you into the End band — the void stretch is silent and clear, whatever the weather is doing back in the overworld.
1.21.1.0.678.0:
### 0.678.0

**Editor menus get an Auto mode and a render-distance dial**

The editor's world-space menus now default to Auto, hiding other plots' panels while you work in one. A new Menu Distance setting on the X-menu caps how far any editor menu draws.

- Auto is the new default for Editor Menus
- New Menu Distance setting on the X-menu (default 128)

### 0.677.0

**One Death Note per target per life**

A second Death Note naming a player you've already noted this life no longer arms a second echo. The repeat book still burns, now telling you they've already been death noted this life. Love Notes follow the same rule, tracked separately from Death Notes.

- One echo per named target per life, not one per note signed
- A repeat note still burns, with a clear message instead of a silent extra echo
- Death Notes and Love Notes are tracked separately, so one of each on the same person still works
1.21.1.0.676.0:
### 0.676.0

**Copy an author's name from the burn line**

In the Book Author Chat line, click the author's name to copy it.

### 0.675.0

**Your builds now upload and can go on the train**

Saving a build in the Train Builder or Train Editor now uploads it to your builder profile, so it follows you between worlds and a finished carriage can be submitted to the train for everyone. Before, "My Builds" told every player that builder profiles were off on their world — the switch shipped off, no server ever turned it on, and so nobody's build was ever uploaded anywhere.

- Uploading still needs Internet Connection on (Options → Dungeon Train), and a build stays private to you until you choose to submit it
- If you deliberately turned builder profiles off, they stay off
- "My Builds" now says when it's your own Internet Connection setting rather than the world's, instead of blaming the world for both

**Spectator cinematic no longer leaves you frozen**

Replaying the intro cinematic from spectator mode could leave you unable to move, with /kill and reboarding the only way out. Fixed. The hotkey can also be switched off now in Options → Dungeon Train…, and it finally shows a readable name in Controls.

### 0.674.0

**Nineteen languages catch up with the game**

Whole features had been reaching non-English players in English: the book-vote replies, the carriage builder, the Free Play and settings-changed notices, the video tools, custom content, and the translation editor's own controls. Every one of the nineteen translated languages now has the full set of the game's text — around 4,460 lines that were simply missing.

- All 19 languages are now complete against English — no missing lines left in any of them
- Newly filled lines are marked as machine translation in the in-game translation editor, so speakers can find and fix them
- Simplified Chinese also gains the two Adventure Item Names buttons it was short

**Keeping your inventory on death is Free Play**

A world that has run with Keep Inventory on is now Free Play — permanently, even if you turn the rule back off.

**The book-author chat line speaks every language too**

The v0.673.0 book-author setting and the Stats Book shipped English-only. Both are now translated into all nineteen languages, along with the chat line that names whoever wrote a book as it burns.

- Book Author Chat, its description, the Stats Book name and the burn line are translated in all 19 languages

**Close the editor's Welcome panel**

The Train Editor's Welcome board now has a close (X) button, top-right. Your choice is remembered per player, per world.

- X button closes the Welcome board
- Editor menu's Welcome Panel toggle brings it back
1.21.1.0.673.0:
### 0.673.0

**See who wrote a book as it burns**

Dungeon Train books burn away after you read them, and until now their author burned with them. Turn on Book Author Chat and every book that catches fire — one you just read, one you threw away unread, one dropped on death — names its writer in chat: "The book by X burns". Off by default; the toggle is in Options > Dungeon Train and in the X menu > Options.

- New Book Author Chat option, off by default
- Credits the author of every Dungeon Train book as it burns
- Per-player: your setting, your chat, on servers too

### 0.672.0

**Discord announcements link to the release they announce**

The release announcement in Discord now opens that exact build's release page. It used to open the Downloads page, which always showed the newest build — so an older announcement sent you somewhere else.

### 0.671.0

**Test the dimensional carriage you're building**

Room authors get a Test the Carriage button in the editor menu. It stamps the dimensional carriage you have open — room, a corridor either side, its own walls mode, block variants, lighting and fog — and puts you in the doorway looking down it. The room repeats around you as you walk, the way it does on the train. Back returns you to the plot and clears it away.

- Shows in the editor menu while a dimensional carriage is open
- No train needed — nothing to ride to and nothing to wait for
- Same tiling, block variants, lighting and fog as the real thing

**Leaving the dimensional carriage editor works again**

Exiting the editor after opening a dimensional carriage directly now returns you to where you came from, in the game mode you were in. Before, it told you there was no session to exit and left you standing in the plot in creative.

- Only affected going straight to a room — /dungeontrain editor portals, or a room plot's Enter Inside
1.21.1.0.670.0:
### 0.670.0

**A book that counts, and a room full of them**

Chests, pots and bookshelves now turn up Stats Books. Open one and it is a coin-flip: either a tall leaderboard, ranking every player on the train and closing on where you stand — or a short note from Faulthurst about your own run, naming one real number from it. You never know which until you read it. Dimensional carriages can now be stocked with the whole tally instead of one author's writing: every leaderboard and every run stat the train keeps, 47 books, shelved in one room with a note on the lectern explaining what you have walked into. Room authors set how often that happens in the Books screen.

- New Stats Book, found in loot — half leaderboard, half a note about your own run
- Leaderboard books moved out of the random-book pool onto their own loot entry
- Dimensional carriages can shelve the complete tally: 29 leaderboards + 18 run stats
- Stats joins Self, Player and Signature as a fourth share in a room's Books mix

### 0.669.0

**The Tallyman's books turn up all over the train**

Leaderboard books are no longer something you mostly find on a bookshelf. They now surface across the train's chests, pots and villager stashes, so a board can turn up wherever you are rather than only where the books are kept. Where a container already offered reading matter, the leaderboard book takes a share of that rather than adding to it, so your odds of finding some book are unchanged — only which book shifts.

- Leaderboard books can now be found in fishing, mining, villager, ore and pottery loot
- Villager stashes get their first book of any kind
- A leaderboard book can appear in the starting chest

**The Free Play badge says why it's on**

Hover the Free Play effect in your inventory and it now tells you what turned it on — the game mode you switched to, the command you ran, a changed setting, a cheat mod it found. Before, that reason was said once in chat and then scrolled away, so joining a world that was already in Free Play left you with a badge and no explanation. The tooltip also got shorter: the reason leads, the consequences fit on one line.

- The Free Play tooltip names what triggered it, including settings changed or cheat mods detected
- The reason survives logging out, so a world you come back to still explains itself

**Container menu now shows item icons**

The container contents menu (C) lists each item by its inventory icon instead of its name, so rows stay compact and long item names no longer spill across the count and weight columns. Click an icon to reveal that item's name beside it; click again to hide it.

- Item rows lead with the inventory icon — narrower panel, no overlapping text
- Click an icon to reveal its name; only that row's column widens

**Faulthurst leaves you a note about your own run**

A new book turns up in the train's loot, signed by Faulthurst. It greets you by name and names one real number from your current life — the carriage you've reached, how long you've been aboard, how many chests you've opened, the longest stretch you went without opening a thing. The number stays live while you carry the book and freezes the moment you read it, so what you find inside is your run exactly as it stood when you opened it.

- Eighteen things he might remark on, twelve of them the one-life half of a leaderboard board.
- He never mentions something that hasn't happened — a number has to be worth a page before he'll write it down.
- Seven ways he opens and twenty ways he signs off, from "Keep it up." to "Why?"
- Written in every language Dungeon Train speaks.

### 0.668.0

**Dimensional carriages can keep their own walls as they repeat**

An endless dimensional carriage used to dissolve its own walls as it repeated — the wall between two copies was carved away so the space read as one continuous hall, taking whatever the builder had put on it with it. Rooms can now be built the other way instead: every copy keeps the walls it was drawn with, and you walk between copies through the doorways the builder left. Existing rooms are untouched.

- New Room Walls setting on a dimensional carriage: Merged (as before) or Kept
- Kept rooms repeat their walls exactly, including the wall the way back to the train stands in
- The library dimension now keeps its walls

### 0.667.0

**Dimensional carriage lighting fades instead of jumping**

Walking into a dimensional carriage no longer snaps the lighting. The corridor now fades once from the light of the world the train is running through to the light of the room at the far end, so crossing between the carriage and its copy is something you feel rather than something you see happen. Turn it off with the new crossingFade client setting.

- One smooth lighting fade along the corridor instead of a jump
- The change is gradual with distance, from the train door to the room door
- Turning around mid-corridor no longer flashes the lighting
- New crossingFade client setting restores the old hard cut

### 0.665.0

Some of the named pigs riding the train answer to a more famous name. A small tribute, and a rare one — you will not meet one every trip.

### 0.664.0

**Paintings now stay put in dimensional carriages**

Paintings and item frames hung in dimensional carriages now stick around properly.

### 0.663.0

**A heads-up when a connection blocker is in the way**

If you run a DPI-bypass tool like zapret or GoodbyeDPI to reach Discord and YouTube, Dungeon Train now tells you once, on the title screen, that it may be sitting between you and brennan.games. Those tools reroute traffic at the driver level, and when they catch DT's traffic the online features don't fail loudly — community books, shared carriages and the rest just quietly never arrive. Now you get told why, instead of wondering where they went.

- One-time notice on the title screen, with a 'Don't show again' if you already know.
- The check is local: it looks at the names of running programs on your own PC, and sends nothing anywhere.
- Only shown if you've allowed the mod to use the network — otherwise there is nothing to interfere with.

### 0.662.0

**The Tallyman's books — 29 leaderboards riding the train**

A new kind of book turns up in chests: a leaderboard, kept by The Tallyman. Each one covers a single board — furthest carriage, longest aboard, most chests opened, kindest benefactors and twenty-five more — lists the top players on it, and closes by telling you where you stand. If you are not on it, it says so rather than inventing a rank for you. Boards that make sense both ways come in a matched pair, one life and all lives, so you can see whether you are good at a run or good at the game. Among the new ones: distance covered, measured from where you started rather than by how far you have paced up and down a carriage.

- Leaderboard books spawn among the train's other random books
- 29 boards, many paired as one-life and all-lives
- Distance covered now measures how far down the line you got, not steps taken
- New boards for people cursed, lovers, most loved, and biggest single gift
- Breaking a vase no longer ends a Walk Past The Loot streak — a vase is not loot
- Every rank gets two lines, so long names are never truncated to fit a score
1.21.1.0.661.0:
### 0.661.0

**Fixed: offhand item duplication**

Shift-clicking a stackable item out of your offhand slot no longer duplicates it. The bug doubled the stack every time and affected every player.
